name: Final Fantasy
credit: Archetypes and signpost uncommons from Wizards of the Coast's FINAL FANTASY Prerelease Guide; each pair's two signposts are legendary creatures from the series. Players' tiers, notes and extra key cards from Draftsim's draft guide (2025), reworded.
about: Players found a balanced, high-synergy and fairly slow format where a cohesive two-color deck wins. Job select, summons and the tiered spells overperformed; most "legends matter" cards did not (Venat is the exception). Payoffs that build up an edge over several turns are what you want.

src.t: FINAL FANTASY Prerelease Guide (Wizards of the Coast)

list.d: Build a big board of artifact creatures, Equipment and Treasure.
list.p: Plays best as a skies deck: fliers early, then countermagic to protect them or stop a bomb later. Draftsim would cut Tidus.

list.d: Get value from the graveyard and win with a slow, steady approach.
list.p: Skip heavy synergy and grind the opponent out with two-for-ones and removal.

list.d: Cast noncreature spells that deal damage to the opponent.
list.p: Build it almost entirely out of removal, using cheap removal to clear away fodder before your edicts.

list.d: Use landfall triggers to pressure the opponent with aggressive creatures.
list.p: Prioritize the best birds and summons; a light splash works with Prishe's Wanderings.

list.d: Build a big board of creatures and tokens, then attack.
list.p: Commit mainly when you have good summons, rares or Rinoa; otherwise black-green or green-blue are usually better homes for the green cards.

list.d: Turn permanents into resources by sacrificing them for payoffs.
list.p: Balance payoffs, sacrifice outlets and fodder, and keep plenty of strong removal.

list.d: Cast expensive spells for extra value, with cards that care how much mana you spent.
list.p: Take noncreature spells that cost four or more mana highly: they are what turn the payoffs on. Led the early win rates among two-color decks.

list.d: Stock the graveyard with permanent cards to power up your spells.
list.p: Town Greeter, Shinra Reinforcements and Resentful Revelation are the backbone; take them highly.

list.d: Equip your best creatures and outvalue the opponent with Equipment.
list.p: Win by building up board advantage with Equipment rather than by racing.

list.d: Play Towns and other nonbasic lands and get extra value from your lands.
list.p: Usually wants at least three colors to support the Towns. Favor removal, big creatures and defensive bodies; bring countermagic in by matchup.
